correctness.rationale: With x fresh its old neighbors are an arbitrary set S. Each old edge internal to S independently allows a new triangle through x, with no higher face constraint. The realizable finite one-point diagrams therefore number Σ_S 2^{e(G[S])}; homogeneity makes a diagram determine the complete type. Each diagram has arbitrarily many realizations by freely taking several copies over A and using the extension property, so precisely these fresh-point types are nonalgebraic. The canonical triangle-filled bases implement comparison of graph isomorphism types within each order, not of arbitrary two-complexes or of different orders. In an independent replay generation by adding a vertex with every possible old neighborhood is exhaustive by deleting a vertex; minimization over degree-compatible labellings removes precisely isomorphisms. This reproduces the class and connected-class counts, verifies no repeats within orders 1–5, and gives exactly the pairs 61/110, 123/685, 927/1751 at values 256, 376, 832. Only the last pair is connected-connected; both of its displayed histograms and all six degree multisets agree.
residual_risks: The enumeration certifies only orders 1 through 6, while the type-count argument works for every finite induced base.

value.rationale: The statistic is motivated independently by extension spaces of a natural homogeneous complex. After removing the automatic old-triangle ambiguity, the first collision is an intrinsic boundary rather than a chosen sample size. The census also distinguishes a substantive obstruction: the scalar loses graph information even on connected bases, and it does so already at the first possible order, despite different induced-edge histograms. These exact smallest examples and the absence of other fibres at that order are useful benchmarks for graph reconstruction by type counts and partition-function evaluations.
residual_risks: No reconstruction theorem for larger orders or for richer type-space invariants follows.
